submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 3 cm thickness is recommended as the optimal choice for the RICH detector. While Radiator-R3 achieves superior pion/kaon separation (4.6σ at 3 cm), it fails the critical humidity ageing requirement and must be disqualified. Radiator-R2 passes the humidity constraint but delivers significantly lower separation performance (2.906σ at its optimum of 2 cm). Radiator-R1 provides the best balance: it passes the humidity ageing test and achieves excellent separation of 3.8σ at 3 cm thickness, which is 30% better than R2's best performance. The 3 cm thickness represents R1's optimal point, offering maximum separation while staying well within the 1-6 cm constraint. This choice ensures reliable long-term operation over the 10-year lifetime while delivering strong particle identification capability.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R1 achieves 3.8σ separation at 3 cm, which is the best performance among radiators that pass all constraints. While R3 achieves 4.6σ, it is disqualified due to humidity test failure.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 is one of the three specified candidates (R1, R2, R3).

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: R1_passes_humidity_constraint = 1, indicating R1 passes the humidity ageing requirement. R3 was disqualified (R3_passes_humidity_constraint = 0).
Recommended thickness of 3 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm.
